title: cli: os audit verify refuses to boot an app that declares queues and assignmentRules ("no 'ownership-queue' service is registered"), same class as #33608 on a different command
body:
## What happens (@objectstack 18.5.0, downstream carbon-black CRM, 2026-11-15)

Found by steedos-labs/os-project-blackcat-crm#113, the deployment and ops manual, which documents audit-ledger verification. The app declares ADR-0142 queues (2) and assignment rules (2), inherited from HotCRM. `objectstack audit verify` exits 2 before reading the ledger:

```
◆ Audit · verify
  ✗ [ObjectQLPlugin] the stack declares queues (2) and assignmentRules (2), but no 'ownership-queue' service is registered, so no queue would resolve and no assignment rule would route a row. Add @objectstack/plugin-sharing to the composition (it registers 'ownership-queue'); the job-queue service named 'queue' is a different service and does not serve ownership queues.
```

- It reproduces on 18.4.0 and on 18.5.0.
- On the same database and app, `objectstack migrate plan` boots and reports the schema in sync. `os serve` runs fine.

## Relation to #33608

#33608 had the same refusal on `os migrate summary-nulls`. Its fix (PR #33879) routes every `os migrate` subcommand through the served-platform composition in `bootSchemaStack`. `os audit verify` has its own boot and was not covered. Other CLI commands that boot the stack outside `bootSchemaStack` may have the same gap.

## Ask

1. `os audit verify` boots a stack that declares queues and assignment rules. Either it composes plugin-sharing, as the served platform does, or it treats queue and assignment-rule metadata as inert for a read-only ledger check.
2. Sweep the other stack-booting CLI commands outside `bootSchemaStack` for the same gap, and fix each one or show it does not need the fix.
3. A regression test runs `os audit verify` on a fixture with one queue and one assignment rule.

## Downstream impact

The ops manual cannot give a working audit-verification step. It currently states the command fails and points here. No app-side workaround is planned; the app will not remove its queues.

Dedupe words: audit verify, ownership-queue, plugin-sharing, CLI boot composition.
